regime_stress_tests.question: Does the fall in lobbying-registrant concentration survive the 2008 semiannual-to-quarterly filing change?
findings: THE DOUBLING IS REAL AND IT IS FILINGS ONLY. Filings go 712 (2007) -> 1,344 (2008), x1.89 - almost exactly the semiannual-to-quarterly factor of 2. Over the same boundary the number of DISTINCT REGISTRANTS goes 135 -> 127, x0.94. More paperwork, the same people. Any 'lobbying activity rose' claim built on filing counts across 2008 is measuring HLOGA.

THE CONCENTRATION TREND SURVIVES THE BREAK. Top-5 registrant share measured on FILINGS falls 28.8% (1999-2003 mean) -> 23.4% (2021-25 mean). Measured on DOLLARS - an instrument HLOGA cannot touch, because a share is scale-free and the same money is reported either way - it falls 54.5% -> 32.9%, a LARGER decline. **The finding is not an artefact of the filing-frequency change.**

TWO CAVEATS THAT STILL TRAVEL WITH IT. (1) The dollar series is volatile in 1999-2003, where annual filings are 397-578 against ~1,200 later, so the early level is a small-N estimate. (2) Report PERIOD length changed at the same date, so per-FILING dollars are not comparable across 2008 even though annual totals and shares are. Quote the share, never the per-filing average.

regime_stress_tests.question: How much of the FY2020-21 assistance spike is COVID relief, measured on dollars rather than row counts?
findings: FY2020: $20.59B against an FY2017-19 mean of $9.56B, an excess of $11.03B. Named COVID relief listings alone account for $7.47B - **67.7% of the entire excess**. Largest single mover: 21.019 'CORONAVIRUS RELIEF FUND' at $7.47B.

FY2021: $40.80B against an FY2017-19 mean of $9.56B, an excess of $31.24B. Named COVID relief listings alone account for $22.07B - **70.7% of the entire excess**. Largest single mover: 21.027 'CORONAVIRUS STATE AND LOCAL FISCAL RECOVERY FUNDS' at $20.23B.

THE FIGURES CORROBORATE THE PUBLISHED ONES. The reported ~$8B (CARES) and ~$20B (ARPA) to tribal governments land on CFDA 21.019 Coronavirus Relief Fund and CFDA 21.027 Coronavirus State and Local Fiscal Recovery Funds in this table at close to those magnitudes. Two independent routes to the same number is the strongest evidence available that the spike is the statute.

AND THE ROW COUNTS WOULD HAVE HIDDEN IT. Assistance rows move 49,195 (FY2020) -> 48,415 (FY2021) - essentially flat, and FY2021 is LOWER - while dollars go $20.59B -> $40.80B. **Relief arrived as a small number of very large transactions.** Anyone sanity-checking this panel on row counts alone would have concluded nothing happened in 2021.

FY2024 IS THE ONE TO WATCH, AND IT IS NOT COVID. FY2024 runs $16.24B against the same baseline, and its top movers are IHS self-governance, Indian Housing Block Grants, Section 8 vouchers, Highway Planning and Grid Infrastructure Deployment - an infrastructure-era composition, not a relief one. That elevation is a CANDIDATE real finding rather than a regime artefact, and it is where the reporting effort should go.

regime_stress_tests.question: Is a prime-contract row count a count of contracts, or a count of administrative modifications?
findings: FY2026: **71.9% of rows with a POSITIVE obligation are $2,500 or less**, median $443. FAR 4.606(a)(1) requires modifications to be reported REGARDLESS OF DOLLAR VALUE, so a row in this table is an ADMINISTRATIVE ACTION, not a contract and not a unit of money.

AND FY2026 IS NOT MERELY HIGH - IT IS AN 8x OUTLIER ON ITS OWN PANEL (9.0% in FY2025 against 71.9%). FAR practice is the standing rule and does not change year to year, so the rule alone does NOT explain this. The leading candidate is the VINTAGE: a partial year captured mid-flight holds the modifications to existing awards without yet holding the new awards those modifications will eventually sit under. That makes FY2026 a PIPELINE fact on top of a REGIME one, and it is the reason FY2026 counts must not be published at all - not merely caveated.

**A CONTRACT-COUNT TREND RUNNING INTO THE RECENT YEARS IS AN ARTEFACT OF REPORTING PRACTICE.** Count AWARDS on a de-duplicated PIID key, or report dollars. Note this compounds with SANITY-04 in docs/CICD_BENCHMARK.md, where no Cedar award key reproduces CICD's 50,167 contracts: the grain question and the micro-modification question are the same question asked twice.
